newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh urged to produce more food.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh urged to produce more food.

text.p: Bangladeshis should work more in agriculture to raise food production for the country's growing population, the head of the U.N. Food and Agriculture Organisation said on Monday.
"We would definitely encourage the people to work in agriculture. The number of people is growing," FAO Director General Jacques Diouf told a news conference.
Diouf said Bangladesh was likely to harvest 20.7 million tonnes of foodgrains this year. "The production is not sufficient...for a country with a population of 120 million," he said.
He said Bangladesh's food security system had gone through a difficult period. "The country has to import grains to make up the deficit," he said.

Diouf said he was happy to see Bangladesh's efforts in using scientific methods and expertise in raising production. "But there is a problem of access to land in this highly populated country. There is also a question of access to credit and marketing," he said.

He said said the growing urbanisation in Bangladesh was a result of problems in the agriculture sector. "If the people living in the rural areas can grow more food and get a better return there will be less influx into the cities," he said.
Diouf said Bangladesh needed to make efforts in crop intensification and diversification for animal farming.
He said: "This is because the production of crops is dependent on the vagaries of nature and soil fertility."
Diouf, who came to Bangladesh on Saturday, met President Shahabuddin Ahmed and Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina.
He said Bangladesh's commitment to agriculture was laudable. "This will certainly help alleviate poverty in the rural areas," he said.
The FAO chief said his organisation was supporting Bangladesh with technical assistance to raise food production and meet protein deficiency through development of fisheries and animal husbandry.
Bangladesh's population is growing at about two percent annually. More than half of the population lives below the poverty line.
Bangladesh earlier said the country's foodgrain production could be 21.03 million tonnes this year.
"Favourable weather during the cropping season has contributed to three percent growth (in foodgrain output)," a recent government report said.
